overview.headline: Computing House apportionment by equal proportions multipliers

keyPoints.point: Primary mandate centers on apportionment of House seats among states
keyPoints.quote: Therein lies the primary mandate of the U.S. census, apportionment of the House of Representatives.

keyPoints.point: All states are given one seat before remaining seats are assigned by priority
keyPoints.quote: Each of the 50 states is given one seat out of the current total of 435.

keyPoints.point: Priority values come from multiplying state population by a multiplier
keyPoints.quote: The priority value is determined by multiplying the population of a state by a "multiplier."

keyPoints.point: Multiplier is divided form using square root of seat number expression
keyPoints.quote: 1 divided by the square root of n(n-1)

keyTerms.gloss: Assigning House seats to states after required enumeration

keyTerms.gloss: Result from multiplying population by multiplier to rank seats

keyTerms.gloss: Factor that falls as seat number rises for priority ranking

keyTerms.gloss: Mean whose reciprocal forms the multiplier base
keyTerms.quote: [which is called the reciprocal of the geometric mean].
